revisions.name: format_is_part_of_the_address
revisions.note: Same bytes as markdown_simple under another format: the ids differ.

revisions.name: crlf_verbatim
revisions.note: CRLF is hashed verbatim — no line-ending folding (unlike messageToken).

revisions.name: lf_counterpart
revisions.note: Same document as crlf_verbatim with LF endings: the ids MUST differ.

revisions.name: untrimmed_whitespace
revisions.note: Leading/trailing whitespace is part of the text — no trimming.

revisions.name: unicode_emoji
revisions.note: Hashed as UTF-8 bytes, astral plane included.

revisions.name: nfc_precomposed
revisions.note: U+00E9. No Unicode normalization: pairs with nfd_decomposed.

revisions.name: nfd_decomposed
revisions.note: e + U+0301, same grapheme as nfc_precomposed: the ids MUST differ.

canonicalJson.name: array_order_preserved
canonicalJson.note: Arrays keep their order; objects inside them are still sorted.

canonicalJson.name: ascii_key_order
canonicalJson.note: Keys sort by UTF-16 code unit and never numerically: "10" comes before "9". For ASCII keys that is also byte order — see astral_vs_bmp_key_order for where the two part ways.

canonicalJson.name: astral_vs_bmp_key_order
canonicalJson.note: UTF-16 code-unit order is NOT code-point order: an astral key starts with a surrogate (0xD83D) that sorts BEFORE U+E000..U+FFFF, while its code point sorts after. A port using byte/code-point order (PHP ksort SORT_STRING, Python sorted) gets these two backwards. Reachable input: report keys come from a user-defined reportSchema.

canonicalJson.name: control_char_escapes
canonicalJson.note: \t \n \" \\ use the short escapes; NUL uses \u0000.

canonicalJson.name: line_separators_raw
canonicalJson.note: U+2028/U+2029 stay raw (PHP escapes them unless JSON_UNESCAPED_LINE_TERMINATORS).

canonicalJson.name: scalars_and_empties
canonicalJson.note: Floats are deliberately absent: no contract payload carries one.

canonicalJson.name: top_level_array
canonicalJson.note: The encoder accepts any JSON value, not only objects.

canonicalJson.name: bundle_hash_preimage
canonicalJson.note: The exact string the es-adversarial bundleHash is the sha256 of.

localeRenders.note: Underscore input is normalized like the dash form.
Case in the stored code does not matter.
Off-grammar legacy code: returned verbatim, never guessed at.

pluralForms._comment: Golden vectors for the plural recipes a gettext-compiling consumer reproduces at DELIVERY time (#486). The WordPress plugin compiles `messages[slug]` to `.l10n.php`, so no ICU renderer runs when a reader loads the page: WordPress picks the form by evaluating the `Plural-Forms` header. That makes two recipes load-bearing — the per-language rule table and the parse of the served ICU — and both fail SILENTLY when wrong (the reader sees the wrong word, or no word, with no error anywhere). `rules` is the table (`gettextRuleFor`), `lookups` the locale resolution (`lookupPluralTable`), `serve` what `renderIcuPlural` puts in a bundle, `parse`/`parseRejects` what `tryParseIcuPlural` recovers from it. Every `serve` message with a non-null value reappears in `parse`, so the two halves are pinned against each other and not just against themselves. Additive: no `messageTokenAlgo` bump — this block describes the RENDERABLE ICU in bundles, which is a different artifact from the canonical form the m1 token hashes. Scope limit, so the block is not read as more than it is: every `serve` vector renders a non-Markdown key. A Markdown key has ` *\n` rewritten to `  \n` INSIDE each body before it reaches the plural structure, so its served bodies differ from what an identical non-Markdown key would carry. That rewrite is orthogonal to everything pinned here — it never moves a selector, a brace or a category.
pluralForms.otherIsMandatory: A value stored as a plural always reaches `messages[slug]` carrying `other`, and the body is non-empty EXCEPT for a language whose gettext rule has no `other` slot at all (`ru`, `pl`, `uk`, `be`), where it is emitted empty and unreachable for integer counts. Presence is guaranteed by OMISSION, not by synthesis and not by rejection: a plural with no usable `other` has its key left out of the bundle, so the reader falls back to the source (#492). SCOPE, because this is the sentence most likely to be over-read: the gate asks its question of the value as a CONSUMER reads it, not of the way it is stored. A source stored as TEXT is walked as an ICU message and refused on the same grounds (#511) — inline `{count, plural, …}` sources are stored as text by design, since the Flutter SDK hashes them opaquely to keep token parity. Walked, NOT pattern-matched as a plural body: `{n, plural, offset:1 other{…}}` is valid and must publish, a plural EMBEDDED in a longer sentence is still judged, `select`/`selectordinal` count too, and `other{}` with an empty body counts as missing. The gettext `ru`/`pl`/`uk`/`be` exception does NOT apply to an inline text: it exists because a stored value gets its `other` branch synthesized on emit, and a text is served verbatim. Two things the gate still does NOT cover: a version published before it existed keeps whatever it froze, and ICU that is malformed WITHOUT missing an `other` (an unbalanced brace) is left alone rather than risk dropping valid copy over a guess. So treat a missing key as untranslated, and keep guarding an empty or absent branch instead of trusting this paragraph.
pluralForms.blankFormsAreAbsent: The rule above is `other`'s case of a general one, and the general one is what a consumer must implement: a plural form is present WITH TEXT, or absent — there is no present-and-empty, for any selector (#510). A form whose body is whitespace-only is dropped on the way out and the served message reads exactly as if its key had never been there; the same goes for a `=N` literal, which is a form like any other. The reason does not depend on the category: `few{  }` renders the empty string, so a reader gets a hole where an absent form would have fallen back to another branch — the `msgstr[2] ""` failure of #490 with a different label. The drop is SILENT on purpose, because a blank form and an absent form are the same state and an absent form is not a diagnostic; a format whose own rule then has a hole still reports it in that format's terms (gettext indexes `msgstr[i]` by slot, so the dropped form surfaces as its empty-slot error). Stored data cannot normally carry one — every door normalizes blanks away — so this is what the RENDERER guarantees about a value assembled in memory, which is the only place one survives. The one thing it does not do is invent: dropping the last non-`other` form leaves a one-branch message, not a synthesized filler.
pluralForms.fallbackIsAGuess: A language with no explicit gettext rule answers with `defaultHeader` and `[one, other]`, flagged `isModelled: false`. The value is declared in one place so consumers cannot each invent a different one; the flag is what makes the guess visible. Two forms rather than one because collapsing to `other` reads as "this language has no singular" and drops the field from the editor, the fill prompt and every export. READ THE RIGHT FLAG: the two tables are NOT the same size — the gettext table states 70 locales, the CLDR table 217 — so `isModelled` (gettext, the rule) and `cldrModelled` (CLDR, the category set) disagree for most of the difference, and 28 of those locales have MORE than two CLDR categories. `isModelled` is the guard a gettext compiler must use. Guarding on `cldrModelled` hands the 2-form default to Slovenian (one/two/few/other) and to Hindi (right categories, wrong boundary for zero) — see the `sl` and `hi` rows in `lookups`.
pluralForms.defaultHeaderLanguagesNote: The languages it is SAFE to hand `defaultHeader` — derived by comparing headers, not by counting categories. `fr` and `pt` are the counterexample the count would miss: two categories, `[one, other]`, but `plural=(n > 1);` — they put 0 in the singular. European Portuguese IS in this list and `pt` is not, from the same primary subtag. These are TABLE KEYS, exactly as in `rules[].lang`: the entry reads `pt-pt`, lowercase, so a direct membership test on a bundle locale answers `false` for `pt-PT`, `pt_PT` and `pt-Latn-PT` — resolve through the `lookups` recipe first. Outside the modelled table this predicate has no answer, and `isModelled` says so instead of implying otherwise.
pluralForms.rulesNote: `forms` is in GETTEXT INDEX order — `forms[i]` is the CLDR category that lands in `msgstr[i]`, i.e. the form the header’s `plural=` expression selects with the value `i`. It is NOT canonical CLDR order. Headers are pinned VERBATIM per language on purpose — several share an expression, and a mutation of the shared Slavic one passed an entire suite that asserted with `contains`. `lang` is a TABLE KEY, not a locale to compare against: keys are lowercase and `-` separated, and one of them (`pt-pt`) carries a region. A bundle locale must be resolved through the `lookups` recipe before it is matched — comparing a locale to these strings directly answers `pt-PT` with nothing and `pt_BR` with nothing. WHY `forms` AND `cldrCategories` DIFFER, and why the difference is not always harmless: for `ru`/`uk`/`be`/`pl` (`other`), `cs`/`sk` and `lt` (`many`) the extra CLDR category covers DECIMALS only, so gettext — which indexes integers — loses nothing. For the rest it is NOT decimal-only and a body IS dropped: `he` carries a CLDR dual reachable at the integer n = 2, and `es`/`it`/`ca`/`fr`/`pt`/`pt-pt` carry CLDR `many` reachable at n = 1000000. `renderIcuPlural` emits those branches into the bundle with NO diagnostic (the drop is reported by the PO exporter, not by delivery), so a compiler walking `forms` silently discards a translated body. Do not read `cldrCategories` minus `forms` as "decimals, safely ignorable".

lookups.note: CLDR states `pt` and `pt-PT` separately; `pt` is the rule Brazil uses and puts 0 in the singular.
European Portuguese puts 0 in the plural — the opposite answer from the same primary subtag.
A region CLDR does not state falls through to its language.
Case and separator are normalized before the lookup.
The REGION is tried before the script is dropped: truncating right-to-left alone would answer `pt-Latn-PT` with Brazil’s rule.
Underscore form resolves identically to the dash form.
Region strip; the third slot stays `many`.
Script strip onto a one-form language.
Unmodelled: both tables answer with the SAME declared fallback, and both say so. A consumer that cannot survive a wrong plural skips the language here rather than applying the default.

A region strip where the region is UN M.49 numeric. It resolves through the plain right-to-left truncation (two subtags), so it does NOT exercise the numeric alternative of the region regex — no table has a dashed numeric key today, which makes that branch unobservable rather than covered. Stated instead of implied.

THE CASE THE OTHER ROWS HIDE: gettext-unmodelled but CLDR-modelled. Slovenian gets the 2-form fallback from the gettext table while the CLDR table gives it FOUR categories — and a served `sl` bundle carries all four. The two flags are not redundant, and `isModelled` (gettext) is the one a compiler must guard on.

The same divergence with the CATEGORY SETS AGREEING, which is why counting categories is not a guard: CLDR gives `hi` exactly `[one, other]`, so the fallback looks right — but CLDR `hi one` is `i = 0 or n = 1`, which puts ZERO in the singular, while the fallback header `(n != 1)` puts it in the plural. Same categories, different boundary, wrong word for 0.

serve.name: two_form_nested_placeholder
serve.note: Bodies keep their own braces. A parser that splits on `}` instead of counting depth loses the placeholder and truncates the message.

serve.name: category_order_is_cldr_not_insertion
serve.note: Emission order is CLDR canonical (zero…other), NOT the order the forms were stored in. A consumer must key on the selector, never on position.

serve.name: literal_selector_first
serve.note: `=N` literals emit before every category, ascending. They are not CLDR categories and no gettext slot maps to them.
serve.message: {n, plural, =0{No files} one{1 file} other{{n} files}}

serve.name: printf_body_travels_verbatim
serve.note: printf bodies cross unchanged: `%1$s` keeps its argnum and `%%` is NOT un-doubled. A formatter that rewrote `%s` as `%%s` reached this seam once already.

serve.name: apostrophe_is_not_icu_quoted
serve.note: The delivered ICU is NOT `canonicalIcu`: apostrophes and braces in a body are literal, never ICU-quoted. Quoting is a hashing artifact and lives only in the token preimage.

serve.name: gettext_complete_language_gets_an_empty_other
serve.note: The bounded exception to the sentence above: ru/pl/uk/be have no `other` slot in their gettext rule, so a fully translated catalog arrives without one. The branch is emitted EMPTY rather than throwing the translation away — unreachable for integer counts in these languages. A consumer must tolerate `other{}` here.

serve.name: incomplete_gettext_language_is_omitted
serve.note: Same language, one slot short: this is a real gap, so the key is left out of the bundle entirely and the reader falls back to the source.

serve.name: missing_other_is_omitted
serve.note: No `other` and no gettext-rule excuse: the key is omitted. It is NOT served as `other{}` — an absent key falls back to the source, an empty branch is a hole in the page (#492).

serve.name: blank_other_is_omitted
serve.note: Presence is judged on the TRIMMED body, not on the key. The doors drop a blank form before it can be stored (#492); this is the in-memory defense behind them.

serve.name: category_outside_the_language_still_emits
serve.note: A category CLDR does not give the language is emitted anyway, with a warning, rather than dropped — a 3-slot `.po` for a 2-form language invents one. Nothing downstream selects it, so a consumer that filters against its own table is right to ignore it; one that trusts the message blindly must not choke on it.
serve.message: {count, plural, one{1 archivo} other{{count} archivos} form2{inventada}}

serve.name: body_edge_whitespace_is_load_bearing
serve.note: A body is emitted BYTE-FOR-BYTE, leading and trailing whitespace included. The door that drops blank forms (#492) does not trim the ones that survive, and only SOURCES are trimmed — a translation is not. A consumer that trims what it parses changes the rendered text.

serve.name: literal_selectors_ascend_numerically
serve.note: Three literals, because one cannot show an order: `=10` sorts AFTER `=2` — the sort is numeric, not lexicographic.

serve.name: unknown_selectors_keep_insertion_order
serve.note: Two unknown selectors, because one cannot show an order: they emit last, in the order the value stored them, NOT sorted (`zform` before `aform`).

serve.name: blank_slot_breaks_the_gettext_completeness_excuse
serve.note: The other half of the ru/pl/uk/be exception, and the half that is easy to lose: the excuse only applies when every slot the rule defines is filled AFTER TRIMMING. A whitespace-only `many` is not filled, so this is an ordinary gap and the key is omitted — it does NOT get the empty-`other` treatment.

serve.name: blank_non_other_form_is_dropped_not_emitted
serve.note: A blank form is not a form, whatever the selector: `few` here is whitespace-only, so the served message reads exactly as if the key had never been there. Until #510 this was the asymmetry a consumer had to tolerate — a blank `other` omitted the whole key while a blank NON-`other` category shipped as `few{  }`, an empty branch that renders a hole. Not reachable through a door (`.normalized` drops every blank form on the way in), so this pins the RENDERER for a value assembled in memory. Note the input keeps the blank: the vector is about what a consumer receives, not about what is stored.

serve.name: blank_literal_selector_is_dropped_too
serve.note: The same rule for a `=N` literal, which is a form like any other. Worth its own row because `=0{}` is the case where the hole is most visible: a literal exists to special-case one count, and an empty one renders nothing for exactly that count. The filled `=1` beside it is the control — the drop is per form, not a decision taken over the literals as a group, and the survivor keeps its leading position.

serve.name: dropping_the_last_non_other_form_does_not_synthesize
serve.note: The bound on the drop: with `one` blank there is nothing left but `other`, and the answer is a one-branch message — not a filler branch, and not an omitted key. `other` carries text, which is the only thing the omit rule ever asked.

parse.name: served_literal_selector_first
parse.message: {n, plural, =0{No files} one{1 file} other{{n} files}}

parse.name: served_category_outside_the_language_still_emits
parse.message: {count, plural, one{1 archivo} other{{count} archivos} form2{inventada}}

parse.name: whitespace_around_selectors_and_commas
parse.note: Whitespace around the head and around each selector is insignificant; whitespace INSIDE a body is not.
parse.message: { count , plural , one {1 file} other {{count} files} }

parse.name: apostrophes_are_NOT_icu_unescaped
parse.note: Bodies are returned verbatim: `''` stays two characters. The parse step does no ICU un-escaping, so it is the exact inverse of the emit step.

parse.name: non_cldr_selector_is_preserved
parse.note: An unknown selector is kept under its own name rather than folded into `other`, so nothing is silently lost.

parse.name: empty_body
parse.note: The empty branch of the ru/pl/uk/be exception, seen from the reader side: it parses to a present key with an empty string.

parse.name: served_body_edge_whitespace_is_load_bearing
parse.note: The reader side of the same rule: the parser returns the body verbatim and does not trim it either. Whitespace around a SELECTOR is insignificant; whitespace inside a body is content.

parse.name: a_blank_branch_in_a_FOREIGN_message_parses_to_a_blank_form
parse.note: No serve twin on purpose — nothing this backend serves looks like this since #510. It is what the recovery parser does with a message written by SOMEBODY ELSE: it reports what the file says, blank branch included, rather than second-guessing it. The blank is then dropped by `.normalized` at the importer door, so it never reaches storage — parse reports, the door decides. A consumer reproducing the parser must not pre-filter here, or it will disagree on a file it did not write.

parseRejects.name: plain_text
parseRejects.note: Not a plural; the caller keeps it as text.

parseRejects.name: placeholder_only
parseRejects.note: Braced, but not a plural head. A consumer must check the head, not the first character.

parseRejects.name: text_containing_a_placeholder
parseRejects.note: Braces inside text do not make it a plural.

parseRejects.name: select_is_not_plural
parseRejects.note: `select` is a different ICU argument type.

parseRejects.name: unbalanced_body
parseRejects.note: A body whose braces never close is rejected, not guessed at.

parseRejects.name: truncated_message
parseRejects.note: The outer brace is missing; rejected before the head is read.

parseRejects.name: selector_with_no_body
parseRejects.note: A selector with no `{…}` after it yields no forms.

parseRejects.name: no_selectors
parseRejects.note: A well-formed head with zero forms is not a usable plural.
